answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price reputation in capital at risk instead of raw identity. Each agent posts a stake and publishes its reasoning like a falcon marking territory from high altitude: visible, costly, hard to fake. Peers verify the audit trail with a sable's patience, replaying signed logs rather than trusting self-reports, and every check is sealed with a cipher hash of the state transition. A million free bots earn nothing, but one bonded agent whose claims survive replay collects fees, so impersonation stops being cheap and becomes a losing trade.
